title: Frugal Sentry: Operational Playbook for Prefetching, Batching, and Quant Profiles
creator: Ravi Shah
body:
Objective: Create an operational playbook and initiative tracker that codifies safe deployments of three primary cost-saving levers (request-level batching, KV/prefix prefetching, and model quantization profiles) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The playbook should include experiment design, gate criteria, rollout order, rollback conditions, customer communication templates, and dashboards for monitoring unit-economics and quality regressions.

Scope: The playbook will cover: 1) candidate selection heuristics for which routes/models to apply each lever; 2) field trial experiment harness and gating; 3) signal taxonomy (latency, p50/p95/p99, token cost, end-to-end error rates, hallucination/semantic-regression checks via eval prompts); 4) automated rollouts via Console runbooks; 5) partner handoffs for Dedicated and Private customers.

Why now: Unit costs rose with broader model usage and several high-volume customers signaled sensitivity to per-token costs. Earlier experiments showed up to 37% token-cost reduction in synthetic batches but surfaced two failure modes: degraded structured-output fidelity (quantization edge cases) and tail-latency regressions when batching and KV prefetch interact. This initiative turns those learnings into a repeatable, safe process that scales.

Acceptance criteria:
- Executable playbook document in Confluence with step-by-step runbooks for canary, A/B, and gradual rollouts.
- Three end-to-end field trials (one hosted public route, one high-throughput enterprise route on Dedicated, one Private customer pilot) completed with pre-defined metrics and an outcome recorded.
- Dashboard widgets in Console for token-cost delta, model-quality regression score, latency SLO breach rate, and rollback triggers.
- Rollout automation recipes (canary traffic split, threshold alarms) committed and merged: GitHub PR links in updates.

Stakeholders: PM (Maya Chen), Eng: Runtime (lead: Kofi Mensah), Infra: Autoscale (lead: Elena Park), Design: UX runbooks (lead: Priya Kapoor), Customer Success: (lead: Aaron Lee).

Notes about trade-offs: Prefetching reduces tokens but increases memory pressure—must cap per-worker prefetch windows by model and profile. Batching increases utilization but can worsen p99 latency; mitigation is smart routing for latency-sensitive routes. Quantization offers large cost improvements but risks subtle generation degradation for structured outputs; guard with per-prompt eval sets and a conservative default profile.

Artifacts: Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ECON/Frugal+Sentry+Playbook, Design spec: https://drive.google.com/design-frugal-sentry, Experiment harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/frugal-sentry-experiments, Console dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/FRUGAL-SENTRY, Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456
milestones: 2026-01-20: Candidate selection heuristics defined; initial route list (40 routes)
2026-02-05: First hosted field trial (batching + KV small-window); results logged
2026-02-18: Quantization safe-profile v0.1 created; internal eval harness tests passed
2026-03-03: Console dashboard prototype live for PM/Eng review
2026-03-12: Canary automation recipes merged (runtime PR #1456); begin Dedicated pilot enrollment
metrics: Primary KPI: average token unit cost reduction (target: >= 20% for grouped population)
Secondary KPI: model-quality regression (acceptance: delta <= 0.5% on eval set; require manual review if >0.5%)
Latency KPI: p95 increase <= 5ms for routes flagged as latency-sensitive; p99 increase must be < 20ms across non-prod workloads
Reliability KPI: no increase in error-rate > 0.1 percentage points for production traffic during pilot
Adoption KPI: % of eligible routes adopting frugal profiles after 90 days (target 30%)
risks: Quantization regressions for structured outputs — mitigation: gated eval suites and opt-out per route
Tail-latency amplification when batching and prefetch interact — mitigation: aggressive canarying and per-route latency budgets
Memory pressure on older GPU instances for large prefetch windows — mitigation: per-instance caps and fallback to no-prefetch mode
Customer trust risk if changes affect outputs — mitigation: customer communications, opt-out toggle, dedicated rollback channels

updates: 2026-01-06: Kickoff meeting happened; hypothesis doc created (Ravi). Action: Maya to curate initial route list.
2026-01-22: Candidate list reduced from 40 to 24 after filtering for latency-sensitive tags and customer opt-in flags (Maya).
2026-01-30: Runtime prototype for small-window prefetch shows 12% cost drop in preprod for one route; memory increased by 6% but within threshold (Kofi).

2026-02-06: Quantization v0.1 passed internal eval for unstructured chat prompts but flagged 1.7% regression on structured JSON outputs — held for manual review (Elena). Decision: exclude structured-output routes from auto-quantization until v0.2.

2026-02-28: Hosted trial final report published: batching+prefetch reduced token cost by 22% for non-structured routes; p99 latency increased by 8ms on average. Recommendation: proceed with canary automation and stricter latency budgets for sensitive routes (Maya).
2026-03-05: Console dashboard prototype demoed to Eng+PM; UX feedback: add per-customer impact drilldowns and one-click rollback. Priya to iterate (Priya).
2026-03-12: Canary recipe PR merged for runtime (#1456). Dedicated pilot invite sent to three enterprise customers; one accepted and scheduled for 2026-03-22 (Aaron).
2026-03-12 (open): Next steps: run Dedicated pilot, finalize playbook docs, and harden quantization safe-profile v0.2 for structured outputs.
review_feedback: Security review (internal): no immediate cryptographic concerns; recommended log redaction for Private deployments (Security Team, 2026-02-10).
Design review: include explicit recovery UX for enterprise admins and a one-click open ticket to CS (Priya, 2026-03-05).
Eng review: preferred rollout order — Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private due to rollback latency and isolation needs (Kofi, 2026-02-12).
final_note: This ticket tracks the initiative-level artifacts and decisions; individual engineering tasks and design tickets live in the referenced ENG/DES issues. Use the playbook for all future cost-optimization rollouts and update it after each pilot to capture edge-case learnings.
